source_user: A service receives a mix of short prompts and long generations. Design an evaluation plan that reports TTFT, TPOT, throughput, queueing, and P99 latency. Scenario variant 101: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: separate prefill and decode behavior; fix workload distribution; report warmup; use repeated trials; capture GPU memory and request-level traces.
corrected_answer: For scenario variant 101, define the comparison as baseline A versus candidate B under a fixed, documented deployment: model and tokenizer revisions, runtime/kernels, hardware topology, precision, parallelism, batching/scheduler, sampling, concurrency, arrival process, prompt/output-length strata, offered loads, SLOs, and correctness criteria. Treat these as assumptions and do not generalize beyond them. Hypothesis: at each prespecified offered load, B changes paired TTFT, TPOT, queue wait, throughput, or P99 end-to-end latency by a practically meaningful, preregistered amount versus A, without unacceptable correctness, timeout, cancellation, rejection, or error-rate regression. Preregister effect thresholds, confidence/uncertainty method, sample size or stopping rule, exclusions, and missing-data handling. Replay the same fixed, stratified request trace with randomized A/B order across repeated independent time blocks on equivalent isolated hosts; warm up separately and report its policy. Capture admission, queue entry/exit, dispatch, prefill start/end, first-token, every decode-token, completion, cancellation, timeout, retry, error, and rejection timestamps. Report queue-inclusive and compute-only TTFT, prefill duration, TPOT as decode time divided by generated tokens (state the zero-token convention), end-to-end latency, request/s and token/s throughput, queue-wait distributions, and P50/P95/P99 by load and prompt/output stratum with explicit denominators. Check output correctness and account for all requests, including failures and timeouts. Collect GPU utilization, memory/HBM, power, clocks, temperature, CPU, host memory, network, cache/paging, batch/concurrency, and scheduler telemetry. Randomization, isolation, trace replay, thermal state, background load, autoscaling, rate limits, tokenization, retries, and cache warmness are confounders; log them and avoid post-hoc cherry-picking. Use paired uncertainty estimates and report measurement limits. Roll back or stop promotion if preregistered latency, throughput, correctness, or error guardrails fail; preserve traces and configuration for independent review. Results are estimates for this setup and require expert review.
risks: Results may not transfer across models, hardware, runtimes, schedulers, workload distributions, or cache states; P99 estimates are sensitive to sample size and tail coverage.
